title: Scaffold app, data layer, week/scoring modules, and integration harness
description:
Read docs/adr/0001-app-architecture-and-scoring-contract.md before starting — it is the authority for every contract below. Stories: S2/S3/S6 foundations. This bead is the wedge's contract core: schema, the two pure single-owner modules, AND the integration harness that proves the database composition.

## Why this bead absorbed contest-wrp.2

Cycle-1 adversarial review of PR #1 returned **REFUTED** with a blocker: the PR introduced the Drizzle schema, migration, and `getDb()` composition while shipping only unit tests, because the integration harness was decomposed into a separate downstream bead. That split structurally violated the standing rule that every code change carries both unit AND integration coverage (and the north star's integration-rank-1 value) — no worker could have satisfied it as originally specified. The harness scope from contest-wrp.2 is therefore consolidated here so the schema lands together with the coverage that proves it. contest-wrp.2 is closed as consolidated.

## Already delivered on branch lane/contest-wrp.1 (commit 007abd0)

Next 16 App Router + TS + Tailwind 4 scaffold, vitest 4 unit config, `src/db/schema.ts` (members / schedule_days / workouts, no unique on workouts member+date), `src/db/index.ts` lazy `getDb()` over `drizzle-orm/node-postgres`, `drizzle/0000_sparkling_shape.sql`, `src/lib/week.ts`, `src/lib/scoring.ts`, and 11 passing unit tests. Do not redo this; extend it.

## Remaining scope

1. **Integration harness** (absorbed from contest-wrp.2):
   - `scripts/test-db.sh`: dedicated Postgres 17 on port **5433** — `docker start contest-test-pg` if stopped, else `docker run -d --name contest-test-pg -p 5433:5432 -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres postgres:17`; wait for readiness. The Supabase local stack owns 54322 on this machine — do not touch it, and do not run any `supabase` command.
   - `vitest.integration.config.ts`: `environment: 'node'`, `fileParallelism: false`, include `tests/integration/**`, `globalSetup` applies drizzle migrations once per session against `postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:5433/postgres`. Same `@` alias as the unit config.
   - `tests/integration/helpers/db.ts`: `pg` Pool + drizzle instance on the same `node-postgres` driver production uses. Document in a comment that integration tests pin time with `vi.useFakeTimers({toFake:['Date']})` — Date only, so pg socket timers are unaffected.
   - `tests/integration/helpers/seed.ts`: per-fixture seed functions returning cleanup closures. `seedMembers(n)` inserts members with bcrypt **cost 4** (fixtures only; production seeding uses a real cost — the contract is any valid bcrypt hash). Never a per-run db reset; a reset alone could eat the whole 30 s budget.
   - `tests/integration/global-teardown.ts`: assert the members row count equals the seeded count after the suite (the members-table-never-grows guard from the ADR test contract).
   - `package.json` scripts: `test:integration` (starts/checks the DB, runs the integration config), `test:all` (unit then integration — this is the 30 s budgeted suite).
   - One README line: contest integration tests assume the `contest-test-pg` container on 5433; only one local stack can own a port.
2. **Canonical-date guard in `src/lib/week.ts`** (cycle-1 review concern, verified): `isEditableScheduleDate` is currently a bare lexical string comparison, so `"2026-8-21" > "2026-08-20"` is true and a non-canonical date passes the freeze gate; `weekStartMonday` feeds unvalidated input to `new Date()`, which silently normalizes `"2026-02-30"` to `2026-03-02`. week.ts is the ADR's single owner of time semantics and the freeze rule rests on it, so both helpers must reject any input that is not a real calendar date in canonical `YYYY-MM-DD` form. Throw a `RangeError` (loud, at the single owner) rather than returning a falsy value that a caller could misread as "not editable".

## Test spec (TDD: write these first, confirm red, then implement)

**`tests/unit/week.test.ts` additions** — keep the 11 existing cases green, add:
- `weekStartMonday("2026-02-30")` throws (calendar-invalid; must NOT return "2026-03-02").
- `weekStartMonday("2026-1-05")` throws (non-canonical: unpadded month).
- `isEditableScheduleDate("2026-8-21", new Date("2026-08-20T12:00:00Z"))` throws — must NOT return true. This is the exact freeze-gate bypass the review demonstrated.
- `isEditableScheduleDate("not-a-date", now)` throws.
- Canonical inputs continue to behave exactly as the existing cases assert (no regression).

**`tests/integration/harness.test.ts`** — the integration proof of the database composition; this is the coverage the review blocker demands. NOT an end-to-end or browser test: no server, no deployed app. (This repository does not run end-to-end or browser tests at all — north star ruling.) Cases:
- Migrations applied: query `information_schema.tables` and assert exactly `members`, `schedule_days`, `workouts` exist in the public schema.
- Schema contract holds against the real database, not just the generated SQL: `workouts` has NO unique constraint on `(member_id, date)` — insert two workout rows for the same member and date and assert both persist (this is the two-a-day rule the ADR requires).
- `schedule_days` composite primary key rejects a duplicate `(member_id, date)` insert.
- `getDb()` composition works through the real driver: obtain it, insert and read back a member, assert the round-trip.
- Seed/cleanup closure: seed a member, assert present, run cleanup, assert gone.
- Running the file twice in a row stays green (idempotent migrations, clean teardown).

## Gotchas

- Timezone math stays on `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with `timeZone: 'America/Toronto'` — do not hand-roll offsets; the existing DST cases will catch it.
- The canonical-date guard must not break `todayInGroupZone`, which already emits canonical output via `en-CA` 2-digit formatting.
- Budget excludes container boot: the suite assumes a warm `contest-test-pg`. The script may start a stopped container; a cold image pull is outside the 30 s.
- `psql` is not installed on this machine — use the `pg` npm package for raw SQL.
- Do not add the fake-Date setup globally; each test file opts in.

## Verification

`npm test` (unit) green including the new guard cases; `bash scripts/test-db.sh` then `npm run test:integration` green, and green again on an immediate second run; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npm run lint` clean. Record the measured `test:all` wall clock against the 30 s budget in the PR.

## Dependencies

None — this is the root bead. It now carries what contest-wrp.2 used to hold.

## File footprint

Existing (extend, do not recreate): package.json, vitest.config.ts, src/lib/week.ts, tests/unit/week.test.ts, README.md, src/db/schema.ts, src/db/index.ts.
New: vitest.integration.config.ts, scripts/test-db.sh, tests/integration/global-setup.ts, tests/integration/global-teardown.ts, tests/integration/helpers/db.ts, tests/integration/helpers/seed.ts, tests/integration/harness.test.ts.

## Acceptance Criteria

Unit suite green including the new canonical-date guard cases (non-canonical and calendar-invalid inputs throw at both week.ts helpers, and the `"2026-8-21"` freeze-gate bypass is closed); integration suite green against real Postgres on 5433 proving migrations applied, the no-unique-on-workouts two-a-day rule, the schedule_days composite PK, the `getDb()` round-trip, and seed/cleanup — green again on an immediate re-run; `tsc --noEmit` and lint clean; measured `test:all` wall clock recorded against the 30 s budget. The cycle-1 review blocker (database composition shipping without integration coverage) is thereby resolved on PR #1.
acceptance_criteria: Unit suite green including new canonical-date guard cases (calendar-invalid and non-canonical inputs throw at both week.ts helpers; the 2026-8-21 freeze-gate bypass closed); integration suite green against real Postgres 5433 proving migrations applied, no-unique-on-workouts two-a-day rule, schedule_days composite PK, getDb round-trip, seed/cleanup; green on immediate re-run; tsc and lint clean; measured test:all wall clock recorded vs 30s budget; cycle-1 review blocker resolved on PR #1
notes: Cycle-1 review resolution, head 8180b0a. TDD evidence: canonical-date guard tests written first in tests/unit/week.test.ts, red run confirmed 3 failing including the 2026-8-21 freeze-gate bypass, then implemented parseCanonicalDate in src/lib/week.ts, green 15/15. Integration: tests/integration/harness.test.ts written first, red confirmed (no integration config existed), then built vitest.integration.config.ts, scripts/test-db.sh, global-setup, global-teardown, helpers/db, helpers/seed, green 5/5. Two guard defects found and fixed: globalTeardown is not a Vitest option so the members-never-grows check was silently never running (tsc --noEmit surfaced it), and a throw from teardown still exits 0 so it was advisory; both verified by deliberately leaking a member row, exit 0 before and exit 1 after. Measured npm run test:all: 4.5s against the 30s budget, 20 tests total. tsc and lint clean. Bead deliberately left in_progress rather than self-closed, pending a cycle-2 verdict, per the gate-inversion finding jotted against abacus.

title: Integration-test harness: dockerized Postgres 5433, two-config vitest, seed/cleanup
description:
Read docs/adr/0001-app-architecture-and-scoring-contract.md (test contract, decision 13) first. This bead builds the integration-test harness every later integration suite runs on. Cross-cutting: serves S1/S2/S3/S6 test coverage.

## Scope

1. Dedicated local Postgres 17 for tests on port 5433 (the Supabase local stack owns 54322 on this machine — do not touch it). Provide scripts/test-db.sh: starts (docker start if stopped, docker run -d --name contest-test-pg -p 5433:5432 -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres postgres:17 if absent) and waits for readiness. The 30-second suite budget assumes a warm container; the script may start a stopped container but a cold image pull is outside the budget.
2. vitest.integration.config.ts (qbrs/twine two-config pattern): environment node, fileParallelism false, include tests/integration/**, globalSetup applies drizzle migrations once per session against postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:5433/postgres.
3. tests/integration/helpers/db.ts — pg Pool to the test DB + drizzle instance (same node-postgres driver as production code paths).
4. tests/integration/helpers/seed.ts — per-fixture seed functions returning cleanup closures (qbrs precedent): seedMembers(n) inserts members with bcrypt cost-4 hashes (fixtures only — production seeding uses a real cost; contract is any valid bcrypt hash), returns {members, cookies?, cleanup}. NEVER a per-run db reset — a reset alone could eat the whole 30 s budget.
5. tests/integration/global-teardown.ts — asserts the members row count equals the seeded count after the full suite (the members-table-never-grows negative-space guard from the ADR test contract; the assertion content lands with the auth bead but the teardown hook file lives here).
6. package.json scripts: test (unit), test:integration (starts/checks DB then runs integration config), test:all (both, sequential — this is the 30 s budgeted suite).
7. One README line: contest integration tests assume the contest-test-pg container; only one local stack can own a port, and 5433 is contest's.
8. Clock discipline documented in a comment in helpers/db.ts: integration tests pin time with vi.useFakeTimers({toFake:['Date']}) — Date only, so pg socket timers are unaffected. Handlers must obtain now via new Date() and pass it into week.ts functions.

## Test spec

[no-test] in the TDD sense for the harness itself — it is test infrastructure; its proof is one smoke integration test tests/integration/harness.test.ts: seed 1 member via seed.ts, select it back through helpers/db.ts drizzle, run cleanup, assert row gone. Estimated cost well under 1 s. This case also proves migrations applied.

## Gotchas

- Migrations in globalSetup must be idempotent across runs (drizzle migrate is; do not drop/recreate).
- psql is not installed on this machine — use the pg npm package for any raw SQL.
- Do not add the fake-Date setup globally; each test file opts in (some cases need real time).

## Verification

bash scripts/test-db.sh && npx vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.ts — harness smoke test green; running it twice in a row stays green (idempotent migrations, clean teardown).

## Dependencies

Needs the scaffold/data-layer bead (schema + drizzle config must exist).

## File footprint

vitest.integration.config.ts, tests/integration/global-setup.ts, tests/integration/global-teardown.ts, tests/integration/helpers/db.ts, tests/integration/helpers/seed.ts, tests/integration/harness.test.ts, scripts/test-db.sh, package.json (scripts section — shared with scaffold bead), README.md (one line — shared)

## Acceptance Criteria

Harness smoke test green twice consecutively (idempotent migrations, clean teardown); seed/cleanup closures verified; members-never-grows teardown hook file exists; no per-run db reset anywhere in the harness; scripts/test-db.sh brings up or reuses contest-test-pg on 5433.
acceptance_criteria: Harness smoke test green twice in a row; migrations applied once per session; seed/cleanup closures work; members-never-grows teardown hook in place; no per-run db reset anywhere
notes: Consolidated into contest-wrp.1 on 2026-08-20. Cycle-1 adversarial review of PR #1 returned REFUTED with a blocker: splitting the integration harness out of the schema bead meant the schema, migration, and getDb composition shipped with unit tests only, violating the standing unit-AND-integration rule and the north star integration-rank-1 value. No worker could satisfy that gate as decomposed. The full harness scope (test-db.sh on port 5433, vitest.integration.config.ts, helpers/db.ts, helpers/seed.ts, global teardown members-never-grows guard, package scripts, README line) now lives in contest-wrp.1 alongside the schema it proves. contest-wrp.3 dependency re-pointed from this bead to contest-wrp.1. Also dropped the smoke-test vocabulary this bead used four times, which conflicted with the north-star ruling that end-to-end and smoke tests are not run here; the harness proof is an integration test and is named as one.

title: Self-auth: sealed cookie sessions, login/logout, seed script, no signup surface
description:
Read docs/adr/0001-app-architecture-and-scoring-contract.md decisions 9-10 first. Story S1 (Identify): a member opens the app on their phone and is recognized with minimal sign-in friction. Acceptance: login once with email+password, stay signed in via persistent cookie, every later request is attributed to that member; no signup path exists anywhere.

## Scope

1. src/lib/auth.ts — sealed HttpOnly SameSite=Lax session cookie (iron-session pattern, SESSION_SECRET env via src/env.ts): verifyLogin(email, password) -> member | null (bcrypt compare); createSessionCookie(memberId); requireMember(request) -> member (throws/returns 401 response on missing/invalid/tampered cookie). Long-lived cookie (~1 year): sign-in is roughly once per phone.
2. src/app/api/login/route.ts — POST, zod {email, password}: 200 + Set-Cookie on success; 401 (identical body) for bad password AND unknown email — no user-enumeration distinction. OUTSIDE the requireMember invariant by definition (ADR decision 9): reachable without a session.
3. src/app/api/logout/route.ts — POST, clears the cookie; does not require a valid session. Known accepted limitation (ADR): sealed stateless cookies cannot be revoked server-side — an old copied cookie stays valid until expiry.
4. src/proxy.ts (Next 16 middleware file) — redirects unauthenticated PAGE loads to /login. Convenience only: the handler-level requireMember is the contract.
5. src/app/login/page.tsx — minimal mobile-first form posting to /api/login.
6. scripts/seed-members.ts — provisions the exactly-three accounts (names/emails/passwords from env or CLI args, real bcrypt cost), idempotent by email. npm script: seed:members (through dotenv-cli).
7. Every LATER mutating handler will call requireMember — this bead establishes the helper and proves the pattern on the auth routes themselves.

## Test spec (TDD: red first) — tests/integration/auth.test.ts, est ~3 s

Fixture: 3 seeded members (cost-4 hashes via harness seed.ts), cleanup closure.
1. Login success: POST /api/login with seeded email + correct password -> 200; Set-Cookie has HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax; a follow-up POST /api/workouts with that cookie is NOT 401 (it may 404/405 until that handler exists — the assertion at this stage is only that auth passes; tighten to 2xx when the workouts bead lands).
2. Bad password -> 401, no Set-Cookie.
3. Unknown email -> 401 with a body identical to case 2.
4. No-cookie table: for every mutating handler that exists at this bead's close (login/logout excluded by definition) a request without Cookie -> 401 and row counts unchanged. Build the table so later beads append their handlers (PUT /api/schedule, POST /api/workouts, DELETE /api/workouts/:id join it in their own beads).
5. Tampered cookie (session=garbage) -> 401, zero rows written.
6. API-surface guard (negative space, mechanical): enumerate src/app/api/**/route.ts on disk; assert the surface equals exactly the ADR decision-10 list intersected with what exists; assert NO path segment matching signup|register|sign-up exists anywhere under src/app.
7. Logout: POST /api/logout with a valid cookie -> clearing Set-Cookie; a request with the emptied cookie -> 401.
Also: flesh out the global-teardown members-never-grows assertion (harness bead created the hook file).

## Gotchas

- Import route handlers directly and invoke with real Request objects against the local test DB — no next dev server.
- bcrypt cost 4 in fixtures ONLY; seed script uses default cost.
- proxy.ts must not intercept /api/* (handlers own their own 401s) — scope its matcher to page routes.
- Do not list login/logout in the case-4 table — they are outside the invariant by ADR definition.

## Verification

npx vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.ts — auth suite green; npx vitest run — unit suite still green; npx tsc --noEmit clean. Full suite time still well inside 30 s.

## Dependencies

Needs the scaffold/data-layer bead (members table, env plumbing) and the integration-harness bead (seed/cleanup, test DB).

## File footprint

src/lib/auth.ts, src/app/api/login/route.ts, src/app/api/logout/route.ts, src/proxy.ts, src/app/login/page.tsx, scripts/seed-members.ts, src/env.ts (shared with scaffold bead), package.json (scripts — shared), tests/integration/auth.test.ts, tests/integration/global-teardown.ts (shared with harness bead), tests/integration/helpers/seed.ts (may gain cookie-minting helper — shared with harness bead)

## Acceptance Criteria

tests/integration/auth.test.ts all 7 cases green including the filesystem no-signup guard and the no-cookie 401 table; login handler reachable without a session; logout clears without requiring validity; seed script provisions exactly three accounts idempotently by email; unit suite still green.
acceptance_criteria: auth.test.ts all 7 cases green incl. filesystem no-signup guard and no-cookie 401 table; login reachable without session; 3-account seed script idempotent

title: Schedule editor (week-replace, strict-future freeze) + workout check-off/undo
description:
Read docs/adr/0001-app-architecture-and-scoring-contract.md (product contract 1-3, decisions 10-11, RECORD amendments) first. Stories S2 (Schedule) + S3 (Check-off), one lane because they share the week-grid UI, validation.ts, and queries.ts. Acceptance: a member declares strictly-future workout/rest days via a week grid, checks off today's workout with one tap, and the freeze rules are enforced server-side exactly as locked.

## Scope

1. src/lib/validation.ts — zod schemas (strict: unknown keys rejected): schedulePut = { weekStart: YYYY-MM-DD (a Monday), days: [{date: YYYY-MM-DD, isWorkout: boolean}] }; workoutPost = strict EMPTY object (a client-supplied date is a 400 — today is always server-computed).
2. src/app/api/schedule/route.ts — PUT, WEEK-REPLACE semantics (ADR decision 10): requireMember; validate; every payload date must fall inside the named week AND be STRICTLY future (isEditableScheduleDate, D > group-zone today) — any violation is a 422 whole-request reject with nothing applied; then in one transaction delete the member's schedule_days rows for the strictly-future dates of that week and insert the submitted days. An omitted future day therefore becomes undeclared — that is how un-declaring works. Today and past days are untouchable through every path.
3. src/app/api/workouts/route.ts — POST, strict empty body: requireMember; insert one workouts row with date = todayInGroupZone(new Date()) server-side. No unique constraint: a second POST the same day is a second row (two-a-days each earn a point).
4. src/app/api/workouts/[id]/route.ts — DELETE (undo): requireMember; 404 if the row does not exist OR belongs to another member (no existence leak); 403 if it is the member's own but dated before group-zone today; else delete. Status contract per ADR decision 10.
5. src/lib/queries.ts — page-read functions only (keep it from becoming a grab-bag): getSchedule(memberId, weekStart), getWorkouts(memberId, weekStart) or equivalents needed by the pages. Score totals arrive with the leaderboard bead. SQL receives date ranges computed in TS via week.ts — never re-derives zone logic.
6. UI: src/components/week-grid.tsx (shared day-grid: 7 columns, workout/rest/undeclared states, disabled for non-editable dates); src/app/schedule/page.tsx (grid editor for current + future weeks, submits week-replace payloads); src/app/page.tsx gains the check-off button for today (shows count of today's workouts, tap to add, undo affordance for today's own entries).

## Test spec (TDD: red first) — amended cases from the RECORD section deltas

tests/integration/schedule.test.ts (~2.5 s), fixture: one member + cookie, clock pinned per case (vi.useFakeTimers toFake Date only):
1. Week-replace: clock 2026-08-20T12:00:00Z; PUT {weekStart:'2026-08-17', days:[{date:'2026-08-21',isWorkout:true},{date:'2026-08-22',isWorkout:false}]} -> 200, both rows present. Re-PUT same week with only {date:'2026-08-22',isWorkout:true} -> 200; 08-22 flipped AND 08-21 row DELETED (omitted future day becomes undeclared).
2. Freeze atomicity: pre-seed frozen row (member,'2026-08-19',is_workout=true). PUT mixing past + future days -> 422; 08-19 unchanged; the future day NOT applied.
3. Today is frozen (inverted from pre-amendment): PUT containing {date:'2026-08-20'} at the same clock -> 422, nothing written.
4. Midnight pair (UTC-bug hunt): PUT {date:'2026-08-21'} at clock 2026-08-21T03:59:00Z (Toronto Aug 20 23:59 — strictly future) -> 200; identical payload at 2026-08-21T04:00:00Z (Toronto Aug 21 00:00 — now today) -> 422. Both instants are already 08-21 in UTC.
5. Outside-named-week date -> 422 whole-reject.
6. Shape: malformed date '2026-8-2' -> 400; isWorkout:'yes' -> 400; zero rows written.
Append PUT /api/schedule to the auth no-cookie table (bead: auth) -> 401 + rows unchanged.

tests/integration/workouts.test.ts (~3 s), fixture: members A and B + cookies:
1. Check-off writes group-zone today: clock 2026-08-20T12:00:00Z; POST {} as A -> 2xx; exactly one new row member A date '2026-08-20'.
2. POST {date:'2026-08-01'} -> 400 (strict empty schema), zero rows.
3. Two-a-day: POST twice -> two rows both '2026-08-20'.
4. Near-midnight determinism: POST at 2026-08-21T03:59:30Z -> row date '2026-08-20'; at 04:00:30Z -> '2026-08-21'.
5. Undo own today: A checks off, DELETE that id as A -> 2xx, row gone.
6. B's row, DELETE as A -> 404, row present.
7. A's row dated '2026-08-19', DELETE as A at clock 2026-08-20T12:00:00Z -> 403, row present.
Append POST /api/workouts and DELETE /api/workouts/:id to the auth no-cookie table; tighten auth case 1's follow-up assertion to 2xx now that the handler exists.

## Gotchas

- The week-replace transaction must be a real DB transaction: the delete+insert pair is atomic, and validation happens BEFORE any write.
- weekStart must itself be validated as a Monday (weekStartMonday(weekStart) === weekStart) -> else 400.
- DELETE undo compares dates in group zone, not UTC.
- Mobile-first UI; keep the grid usable on a phone screen. No e2e tests exist — UI correctness is manual-use territory; server contracts carry the tests.

## Verification

npx vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.ts green; npx vitest run green; npx tsc --noEmit clean; record actual suite wall-clock next to the 30 s budget in the PR description.

## Dependencies

Needs the auth bead (requireMember, cookie fixtures), the harness bead, and the scaffold bead.

## File footprint

src/lib/validation.ts, src/lib/queries.ts, src/app/api/schedule/route.ts, src/app/api/workouts/route.ts, src/app/api/workouts/[id]/route.ts, src/components/week-grid.tsx, src/app/schedule/page.tsx, src/app/page.tsx (shared with scaffold + leaderboard beads), tests/integration/schedule.test.ts, tests/integration/workouts.test.ts, tests/integration/auth.test.ts (appends to the no-cookie table — shared with auth bead)

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Weekly leaderboard with missed-day chips and zero-score visibility
description:
Read docs/adr/0001-app-architecture-and-scoring-contract.md (product contract 2, decisions 11-13) first. Story S6 (Leaderboard), wedge slice: the WEEKLY race only — the all-time tally is post-wedge and must NOT be built here. Acceptance: any member opens the app and sees, at a glance, all three members' current-week points and who is winning, with missed declared days visible, computed entirely server-side.

## Scope

1. src/lib/queries.ts additions (this bead extends the file the schedule bead created — sequential dependency, not a parallel lane): weeklyScores(weekStart) -> [{memberId, name, points}] for ALL members — computed in SQL (count of workouts rows in [weekStart, weekStart+7) joined against members). CRITICAL preserved guarantee (ADR decision 13): a member with zero workouts appears with points 0, never absent — LEFT JOIN from members, not GROUP BY over workouts. missedDaysFor(memberId, weekStart, now) may delegate the day-set arithmetic to scoring.ts missedDays over fetched rows. There is NO dual scoring path and NO SQL-vs-reference parity assertion (ADR decision 11) — the SQL read path is the implementation; scoring.ts contributes POINTS_PER_WORKOUT and missedDays only.
2. src/components/leaderboard.tsx — ranked list; equal points display as ties (equal rank, no hidden tiebreaker); per-member missed-day chips (the ribbing surface); zero-score members fully visible.
3. src/app/page.tsx — home page becomes: this week's leaderboard + the check-off button (from the schedule/check-off bead). Server component reads via queries.ts.
4. Week ranges computed in TS via week.ts and passed to SQL as parameters — SQL never re-derives zone logic.

## Test spec (TDD: red first) — tests/integration/scores.test.ts (~2.5 s)

Fixture: 3 members; clock 2026-08-20T12:00:00Z. Per the RECORD deltas the dual-path equality assertion is REMOVED; assert expected values through the SQL read path only:
1. Seed: member1 rows 2026-08-17, 2026-08-19, 2026-08-19 (two-a-day), 2026-08-16 (prior ISO week); member2 rows 2026-08-18, 2026-08-23 (Sunday — still week 2026-08-17); member3 none. weeklyScores('2026-08-17') -> member1 = 3, member2 = 2, member3 = 0 AND member3 is PRESENT (the zero-score guarantee).
2. Tie: bring members 1 and 2 to equal points -> equal rank, both shown, no tiebreak ordering asserted.
3. missedDays through the seam: schedule fixture from the unit case (Mon workout done, Tue workout missed, Wed rest, Thu today) seeded into real tables -> missed = exactly ['2026-08-18']; points unaffected (display-only, never a penalty).
4. Week-window: rows 2026-07-06 and 2026-08-17 -> weeklyScores('2026-08-17') counts only 1 for that member. (All-time totals are post-wedge — no all-time assertion exists in this suite.)

## Gotchas

- LEFT JOIN members -> workouts, or a members-driven subquery; a plain GROUP BY workouts.member_id silently drops the zero-score friend and still passes naive assertions — this is the exact bug the preserved guarantee targets.
- Sunday belongs to the week begun the previous Monday (ISO) — the 2026-08-23 row is in week 2026-08-17.
- Do not add caching (ADR decision 12: per-request reads, strong consistency).

## Verification

npx vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.ts green; npx vitest run green; npx tsc --noEmit clean; report the measured full-suite wall clock against the 30 s budget — this bead completes the wedge suite (~44 cases, est ~16 s).

## Dependencies

Needs the schedule/check-off bead (queries.ts exists, workout/schedule data paths live), and transitively auth + harness + scaffold.

## File footprint

src/lib/queries.ts (shared with schedule/check-off bead — sequenced by dependency), src/components/leaderboard.tsx, src/app/page.tsx (shared with scaffold + schedule/check-off beads), tests/integration/scores.test.ts

## Acceptance Criteria

scores.test.ts green through the SQL read path only: weekly 3/2/0 with the zero-score member PRESENT, ties as equal rank, Sunday row counted in the prior-Monday week, missedDays exactly [2026-08-18] with points unaffected, week-window exclusion; no all-time tally anywhere; measured full-suite wall clock recorded against the 30s budget in the PR.
acceptance_criteria: scores.test.ts green: SQL-path expected values 3/2/0 with zero-score member PRESENT, ties as ties, ISO Sunday in prior week, missedDays through the seam; no all-time tally built; measured full-suite wall clock recorded vs 30s budget

title: Provision and deploy: Vercel Hobby scope, Neon integration, prod seed (OPERATOR-IN-LOOP)
description:
Read docs/adr/0001-app-architecture-and-scoring-contract.md decisions 6-7 first. Cross-cutting: puts the completed wedge (S1+S2+S3+S6) on real phones. DELIBERATELY DEFERRED and OPERATOR-IN-THE-LOOP: it requires the operator's Vercel account choice, Neon provisioning consent, and the three members' real emails/passwords. An autonomous drain must NOT pick this up; it leaves the ready front via deferred status until the operator activates it.

## Scope

1. vercel link under the OPERATOR'S PERSONAL HOBBY SCOPE (ADR decision 6 — NOT the Pro team org team_k4wULKWTqJv6rtKbwpu2posh: Blob free allotments exist only on Hobby, and the free-stack ruling depends on it).
2. vercel integration add neon (marketplace, auto-provisions DATABASE_URL into the project; free plan). Push drizzle migrations against the provisioned instance (dotenv-cli + drizzle-kit migrate, using vercel env pull .env.local).
3. Set SESSION_SECRET in Vercel env (generate, never commit).
4. Run scripts/seed-members.ts against production with the three real accounts (operator supplies names/emails/passwords at run time — never store them in the repo or the tracker).
5. vercel deploy to production; verify login + check-off + leaderboard on a real phone (manual use — the no-e2e ruling makes this the human step).
6. README: one deploy section (scope, env vars, seed command).

## Test spec

[no-test]: deployment/configuration only — no code paths change; the wedge suite already gates the code. The manual phone walk-through in step 5 is the acceptance check, per the north star's no-e2e ruling.

## Gotchas

- vercel link defaults to the last-used scope — verify the personal scope explicitly before confirming.
- Neon pooled vs direct URL: the app uses the pooled TCP URL with the pg driver (ADR decision 7); drizzle-kit migrate wants the direct (non-pooled) URL — the integration provisions both.
- Cold starts after idle (~hundreds of ms) are expected Neon scale-to-zero behavior, not a bug (ADR decision 12).

## Verification

vercel deploy succeeds; all three members can log in on their phones; a check-off appears on the leaderboard; git status clean and pushed.

## Dependencies

Needs the leaderboard bead (the wedge must be complete and green locally first).

## File footprint

.vercel/ (gitignored link metadata), README.md (deploy section — shared), package.json (possible deploy helper script — shared), .env.example (SESSION_SECRET, DATABASE_URL documented — shared with scaffold bead)

## Acceptance Criteria

Deployed under the personal Hobby scope (verified, not defaulted); Neon provisioned via vercel integration add neon; migrations applied to prod; SESSION_SECRET set; three real accounts seeded without credentials entering repo or tracker; all three members log in and check off on real phones; README deploy section present. [no-test]: config/deploy only.
acceptance_criteria: Deployed under personal Hobby scope; Neon provisioned via marketplace; migrations pushed; 3 real accounts seeded; all three members log in and check off on real phones. [no-test]: config/deploy only, wedge suite already gates the code
